name: woob
why: Scrapes and drives websites through backend modules, a door into how web services can be treated as APIs, though it leans toward plumbing.

brief.what_it_is: woob (Web Outside of Browsers) is a collection of applications that interact with websites without requiring the user to open them in a browser. It also provides well-defined APIs to talk to websites that lack one. The homepage lists graphical Qt apps such as video-qt, housing-qt, job-qt, recipes-qt, msg-qt and dating-qt, plus command-line and scripting interfaces for the same capabilities. The page does not spell out exactly what goes in or what comes out, but the examples suggest it takes search terms or account actions and returns things like videos, job offers, recipes, lyrics, messages and bank balances.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to get information faster, script around websites to automate tasks, extend what websites can do, and help blind people use poorly built websites. It also pitches reuse of favourite applications across many sites, without learning a separate interface for each one.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says woob is written in Python and leverages, but is not limited to, Requests and lxml, with Qt for graphical applications and git for collaboration. It describes continuous integration that notifies developers when a website has changed, and an update system that pushes fixes quickly to end users. The per-site internals are not explained on the homepage.
brief.install_notes: The homepage shows a GET WOOB button for version 3.7, released Tuesday 29 October 2024, but the page gives no install commands, runtime requirements or first-run steps. The brew metadata lists the executable as woob. Beyond brew install, I could not confirm any setup from the homepage alone.
brief.standout: Instead of one scraper per site, woob ships many per-site backends behind shared capability interfaces, so the same kind of task works across different sites and can be driven from a GUI, a terminal or a script. The continuous integration that flags when a site changes is also a notable part of the pitch.
brief.status: Maintained, by the evidence on the homepage. It says Actively developed, has a 3.7 release dated 29 October 2024, and lists 208 contributors with thousands of patches. I did not check a repository commit log, so the exact date of the latest commit is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not state supported platforms, and the Qt apps imply a desktop environment. Many backends depend on third-party websites, so they will break whenever a site changes its layout, which is the reason the project runs CI to catch this. The project is LGPL licensed. The homepage does not describe any missing features or known limitations, and I did not fetch the docs or repository, so this brief covers only the homepage.
quotes: woob is a collection of applications able to interact with websites, without requiring the user to open them in a browser.
Continuous integration notifies developers if a website has changed
It helps blind people use crappy websites
Use your mail client to troll on your favorite websites!
